facts.statement: Alamosaurus is a genus of dinosaur.
facts.quote: taxon: Alamosaurus

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Alamosaurus is Alamosaurus sanjuanensis.
facts.quote: type_species: Alamosaurus sanjuanensis

facts.statement: Alamosaurus was described by Charles Whitney Gilmore in 1922.
facts.quote: authority: Gilmore, 1922

facts.statement: Alamosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically the Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian)

facts.statement: Alamosaurus fossils are found in what is now southwestern North America.
facts.quote: from the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous period in what is now southwestern North America

facts.statement: Alamosaurus is one of the few sauropods known to have lived in North America after a 30-million-year gap in the fossil record.
facts.quote: It is one of the only known sauropods to have inhabited North America after the nearly 30-million-year absence of sauropods from the continent's fossil record

facts.statement: Researchers suggest Alamosaurus likely migrated to North America from either South America or Asia.
facts.quote: probably represents an immigrant from South America or Asia

facts.statement: Adult Alamosaurus measured approximately 26 meters in length, 5 meters tall at the shoulder, and weighed between 30 and 35 tonnes.
facts.quote: Adults would have measured around 26 m long, 5 m tall at the shoulder and weighed up to 30 - 35 t

facts.statement: The holotype of Alamosaurus was discovered in June 1921 by Gilmore, Reeside, and Sternberg in New Mexico.
facts.quote: The holotype was discovered in June 1921 by Charles Whitney Gilmore, John Bernard Reeside, and Charles Hazelius Sternberg at the Barrel Springs Arroyo in the Naashoibito Member of the Ojo Alamo Formation

facts.statement: Gilmore originally described the holotype as a left scapula and the paratype as a right ischium in 1922.
facts.quote: Smithsonian paleontologist Gilmore originally described holotype USNM 10486, a left scapula (shoulder bone), and the paratype USNM 10487, a right ischium (pelvic bone) in 1922

facts.statement: The name Alamosaurus is not derived from the Alamo mission or battle in San Antonio, Texas.
facts.quote: the dinosaur is not named after the Alamo in San Antonio, Texas, or the battle that was fought there

facts.statement: The name Alamosaurus is derived from the Ojo Alamo geologic formation where the fossils were found.
facts.quote: Instead, the name Alamosaurus comes from Ojo Alamo, the geologic formation in which it was found

facts.statement: The word 'alamo' is Spanish for 'poplar' and refers to a local subspecies of cottonwood tree.
facts.quote: The term alamo itself is a Spanish word meaning "poplar" and is used for the local subspecies of cottonwood tree

facts.statement: The species name sanjuanensis refers to San Juan County, New Mexico, where the first remains were discovered.
facts.quote: There is only one species in the genus, Alamosaurus sanjuanensis, which is named after San Juan County, New Mexico, where the first remains were found

facts.statement: Gilmore posthumously described specimen USNM 15560 in 1946, which was found in Utah in 1937.
facts.quote: In 1946, Gilmore posthumously described a more complete specimen, USNM 15560, found on June 15, 1937, on the North Horn Mountain of Utah by George B. Pearce

facts.statement: In 2025, Gregory S. Paul reclassified USNM 15560 as the holotype of the new genus Utetitan.
facts.quote: In 2025, Gregory S. Paul assigned USNM 15560 as the holotype of the new taxon Utetitan zellaguymondeweyae

facts.statement: The Perot Museum's Alamosaurus mount is a composite reconstruction based on multiple titanosaur specimens.
facts.quote: The restored Alamosaurus skeletal mount at the Perot Museum was based on a composite of several titanosaur specimens found in Late Cretaceous rocks of North America

facts.statement: Alamosaurus was a large, four-legged herbivore with a long neck, long tail, and partial bony armor.
facts.quote: Alamosaurus was a gigantic quadrupedal herbivore with a long neck, a long tail, relatively long limbs and a body partly covered with bony armor

facts.statement: Alamosaurus uniquely possesses pneumatic ribs extending for two-thirds of their length among titanosaurs.
facts.quote: Uniquely among titanosaurs, the ribs of Alamosaurus are pneumatised for two-thirds of the rib length

facts.statement: Trackway evidence indicates Alamosaurus walked slowly at 3.2 to 4 km/h without dragging its tail.
facts.quote: Trackways show that Alamosaurus walked slowly at speeds of 3.2 – 4 km/h without dragging their tails

facts.statement: Studies estimate Alamosaurus growth lines formed between 4 and 12 years, with a maximum lifespan of 55 years.
facts.quote: Lehman and Woodward estimated that the growth lines of Alamosaurus were drawn at 4–12 years, and the maximum age of Alamosaurus was 55 years for the age at 90% of the mass

facts.statement: It is debated whether fossils from formations like the North Horn, Black Peaks, and Javelina belong to Alamosaurus or a distinct genus.
facts.quote: though these specimens may represent a distinct genus

facts.statement: A 2025 study proposed that USNM 15560 belongs to a new genus, Utetitan, rather than Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: In 2025, Gregory S. Paul assigned USNM 15560 as the holotype of the new taxon Utetitan zellaguymondeweyae

facts.statement: Scientists debate whether a massive tibia found in the North Horn Formation belongs to Alamosaurus or a new sauropod species.
facts.quote: Scott Hartman estimates Alamosaurus, based on a huge incomplete tibia that probably refers to it, being slightly shorter at 28 - 30 m and equal in weight to other massive titanosaurs, such as Argentinosaurus and Puertasaurus, though he states that scientists do not know whether the massive tibia belongs to an Alamosaurus or a completely new species of sauropod

facts.statement: Friedrich von Huene classified Alamosaurus within the family Titanosauridae in 1927.
facts.quote: In 1927, Friedrich von Huene placed it in Titanosauridae.

facts.statement: Some phylogenetic analyses group Alamosaurus with Opisthocoelicaudia in the subgroup Opisthocoelicaudiinae of Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: One major analysis unites Alamosaurus with Opisthocoelicaudia in the subgroup Opisthocoelicaudiinae of Saltasauridae.

facts.statement: Other studies place Alamosaurus as a sister taxon to Pellegrinisaurus, outside the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: A major competing analysis finds Alamosaurus as a sister taxon to Pellegrinisaurus, with both genera located just outside Saltasauridae.

facts.statement: A 2022 analysis by Navarro and colleagues recovered Alamosaurus as a member of Saltasauridae, specifically as the sister taxon to Baurutitan.
facts.quote: In 2022, Navarro and colleagues included Alamosaurus in their phylogenetic analysis of titanosaurs. Their results placed BIBE 45854, a series of neck vertebrae traditionally assigned to Alamosaurus, in a position distantly related to Alamosaurus itself; the vertebrae were recovered within the Lognkosauria, while Alamosaurus was recovered as a member of the Saltasauridae, as the sister taxon to Baurutitan:

facts.statement: The earliest fossils of Alamosaurus date to around 70 million years ago, and it became the dominant large herbivore in southern Laramidia.
facts.quote: The earliest fossils of Alamosaurus date to the Maastrichtian age, around 70 million years ago, and it rapidly became the dominant large herbivore of southern Laramidia.

facts.statement: A third hypothesis proposes that Alamosaurus originated in Asia rather than South America.
facts.quote: A third option is that, as in the austral immigrant scenario, Alamosaurus is not native to North America, but originated in Asia instead of South America.

facts.statement: Alamosaurus fossils are notably found in the Naashoibito Member of the Ojo Alamo Formation, dated to approximately 66.87 million and 66.38 million years ago.
facts.quote: Alamosaurus fossils are most notably found in the Naashoibito Member of the Ojo Alamo Formation (or Kirtland Formation), dated to 66.87 ± 0.04 Ma and 66.38 ± 0.08 Ma around 5 metres (16 ft) and 3.5 metres (11 ft) above the base of the member respectively.

facts.statement: The Alamosaurus fauna is dated to the latest Maastrichtian age.
facts.quote: The Alamosaurus fauna can be dated to the latest Maastrichtian age.

facts.statement: The association of Alamosaurus and Quetzalcoatlus likely inhabited semi-arid inland plains.
facts.quote: The Alamosaurus-Quetzalcoatlus association probably represent semi-arid inland plains.

facts.statement: Fossils of Alamosaurus from the Evanston Formation in Wyoming indicate it shared its environment with Triceratops.
facts.quote: Fossils of Alamosaurus unearthed in the Evanston Formation in Wyoming indicate it shared its environment with Triceratops.

facts.statement: Definitive fossils of Alamosaurus sanjuanensis come from the Ojo Alamo Formation.
facts.quote: Definitive specimens of Alamosaurus sanjuanensis are known from the Ojo Alamo Formation.

facts.statement: Specimens previously attributed to Alamosaurus from the North Horn, Black Peaks, and Javelina Formations were reassigned to the genus Utetitan in 2025.
facts.quote: Previously referred specimens from the North Horn Formation, the Black Peaks Formation and possibly the Javelina Formation have been assigned to Utetitan in 2025.

facts.statement: The genus Alamosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1922.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Gilmore, 1922

facts.statement: The species Alamosaurus sanjuanensis was named by Gilmore in 1922.
facts.quote: species_authority: Gilmore, 1922

facts.statement: Alamosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Cretácico superior

facts.statement: Alamosaurus lived approximately 70 to 66 million years ago during the late Maastrichtian stage of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 70 y 66 millones de años, a fines del Maastrichtiense

facts.statement: Alamosaurus lived in what is now North America.
facts.quote: en lo que hoy es Norteamérica

facts.statement: Alamosaurus is the only described North American titanosaur from the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Es el único titanosauriano norteamericano descrito de finales del Cretácico

facts.statement: Adult Alamosaurus are estimated to have reached about 26 meters in length, 5 meters in height at the shoulders, and weighed up to 30 to 35 tonnes.
facts.quote: Los adultos habrían medido alrededor de 26 metros de largo, 5 metros de alto hasta los hombros y pesaron hasta 30-35 toneladas

facts.statement: Fossils found near the K/T boundary make Alamosaurus one of the last recorded titanosaurians before the mass extinction event.
facts.quote: Sus restos han sido hallados en formaciones rocosas muy cercanas al Límite K/T, por lo que fue uno de los últimos titanosaurios registrados hasta el suceso de la extinción masiva del Cretácico-Paleógeno

facts.statement: Alamosaurus had a small head supported by a long, robust neck, a broad and bulky torso, cylindrical legs for weight support, and a relatively slender tail for balance and locomotion.
facts.quote: Como saurópodo, tenía una cabeza pequeña, sostenida por un largo y robusto cuello, con un torso amplio y corpulento, patas cilíndricas para soportar su peso y una cola, relativamente esbelta, para ayudarle en el equilibrio y coordinación locomotora.

facts.statement: The general appearance of Alamosaurus resembles Brachiosaurus more than Diplodocus.
facts.quote: Su aspecto general llegaría a recordar más a Brachiosaurus que a Diplodocus.

facts.statement: Alamosaurus was a giant quadrupedal herbivore with long necks and tails and relatively long legs.
facts.quote: Alamosaurus fue un herbívoro cuadrúpedo gigante con un cuello y colas largos y patas relativamente también largas.

facts.statement: Alamosaurus is known for having multiple specimens preserved in various states of completeness, which is uncommon for large titanosaurians.
facts.quote: Alamosaurus es conocido por restos de varios especímenes en diferentes estados de preservación, situación no muy común en titanosaurios de mediano y gran tamaño.

facts.statement: Partial adult skeletons suggest Alamosaurus measured between 20 and 24 meters long, 12 meters high to the head, and weighed between 32.7 and 50 tonnes.
facts.quote: Varias muestras adultas, conocidas por esqueletos parciales, se estiman que midieron entre 20 y 24 metros de longitud, 12 m de altura hasta la cabeza y entre 32,7 y 50 toneladas de peso.

facts.statement: Thomas Holtz proposed that the largest adults could have reached over 30 meters in length and weighed between 72.5 and 80 tonnes or more.
facts.quote: Thomas Holtz propuso una longitud máxima de alrededor de 30 metros o más y un peso aproximado de 72,5 a 80 toneladas o más.

facts.statement: Exceptional fragmentary remains found in Chihuahua, Mexico, include a broken tibia estimated at 165 cm long, attributed to Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: También se han hallado restos fragmentarios, de tamaños excepcionales, en Chihuahua, México, que se atribuyen al género Alamosaurus, los vestigios corresponderían a una tibia rota estimada en 165 cm de largo.

facts.statement: Scientists have not yet agreed on whether the massive tibia found in Mexico belongs to Alamosaurus or a completely new sauropod species.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, por el momento, los científicos no se han puesto de acuerdo si la masiva tibia pertenece a un Alamosaurus o una especie completamente nueva de saurópodo.

facts.statement: Although no skull has been found, stick-shaped teeth associated with Alamosaurus skeletons likely belonged to this dinosaur.
facts.quote: Aunque ningún cráneo ha sido encontrado, los dientes en forma de bastoncillos se han encontrado asociados a esqueletos de Alamosaurus y probablemente pertenecía a este dinosaurio.

facts.statement: Alamosaurus had lateral fossae in its vertebrae resembling shallow depressions.
facts.quote: Alamosaurus tenía fosas laterales en las vértebras que se parecen a depresiones poco profundas.

facts.statement: The presence of osteoderms was recently confirmed in Alamosaurus, forming an organic armor distributed across its back useful for defense against predators.
facts.quote: la presencia de osteodermos fueron confirmados en este género recientemente, estructura orgánica distribuida a lo largo y ancho del dorso del animal, muy útil como armadura defensiva ante el ataque de depredadores.

facts.statement: Alamosaurus had more robust radius bones than Venenosaurus.
facts.quote: Alamosaurus tenía radios más robustos que los de Venenosaurus.

facts.statement: A possible specimen of Alamosaurus coexisted with dinosaurs such as Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis and Sierraceratops from the McRae Group.
facts.quote: A possible specimen of the genus identified as Alamosaurus sp. or cf. Alamosaurus coexisted with dinosaurs such as Tyrannosaurus mcraeensis and Sierraceratops from the McRae Group.

facts.statement: In 1946, a more complete skeleton was found in Utah, consisting of a complete tail, a complete right forelimb except for the foot tip, and both ischia.
facts.quote: En 1946, encontró un esqueleto más completo en Utah, consistiendo en una cola completa, un miembro anterior derecho completo excepto por el extremo del pie y ambos isquiones

facts.statement: In 2015, it was confirmed that a previously described specimen included osteoderms, marking the first confirmation that these structures were present in Alamosaurus.
facts.quote: En 2015 se mostró que este espécimen, el cual ya había sido descrito, también incluía osteodermos, la primera confirmación de que estos estaban presentes en Alamosaurus

facts.statement: Fossils of Alamosaurus have been found in formations dating from approximately 74 million years ago to the end of the Cretaceous, 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Estas formaciones de hace aproximadamente 74 millones hasta el final del Cretácico hace 66 millones de años

facts.statement: The fauna associated with Alamosaurus appears to have existed between 70 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: La fauna asociada a Alamosaurus parece haber durado entre 70 a 66 millones de años

facts.statement: Alamosaurus belongs to the Macronaria group of Sauropoda, a classification that explains its robust anatomy, forelimbs higher than hindlimbs, and a tail slightly smaller relative to the rest of the body.
facts.quote: Pertenece al grupo Macronaria de Sauropoda, clasificación taxonómica que explica su anatomía robusta, extremidades delanteras más altas que las traseras y una cola ligeramente más pequeña en relación con el resto del cuerpo

facts.statement: In 1927, Friedrich von Huene classified Alamosaurus within the Titanosauridae family.
facts.quote: En 1927 Friedrich von Huene lo colocó en el Titanosauridae

facts.statement: An important analysis united Alamosaurus with Opisthocoelicaudia in the subfamily Opisthocoelicaudiinae of the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Un análisis importante une a Alamosaurus con Opisthocoelicaudia en una subfamilia Opisthocoelicaudiinae de la familia Saltasauridae

facts.statement: A recently published analysis by Anthony Fiorillo & Ron Tykoski et al. indicates that Alamosaurus was a sister taxon to Lognkosauria and therefore close to dinosaurs such as Futalognkosaurus and Mendozasaurus outside of Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Un análisis recientemente publicado Anthony Fiorillo & Ron Tykoski et al indica que Alamosaurus era un taxón hermano a la Lognkosauria y por lo tanto cercano a dinosaurios tales como Futalognkosaurus y Mendozasaurus por fuera de saltasauridae

facts.statement: The parent group of Alamosaurus is Saltasaurinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Saltasaurinae

facts.statement: Alamosaurus belongs to the family Saltasauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Saltasauridae

facts.statement: Alamosaurus is classified in the class Saurischia.
facts.quote: Class: Saurischia

facts.statement: Alamosaurus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian stages, from 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The most complete known specimen is a recently discovered juvenile skeleton in Texas, which allowed for accurate estimates of length and mass.
facts.quote: El espécimen más completo conocido es un esqueleto juvenil recientemente descubierto en Texas, que permitió estimaciones correctas de la longitud y masa

facts.statement: The genus and species were named by Smithsonian paleontologist Charles W. Gilmore in 1922.
facts.quote: El género y la especie fueron nombrados por el paleontólogo del Smithsoniano, Charles W. Gilmore en 1922
